A capitalized name says "component". If you call a component as a plain function, React doesn't know it's there. Its hooks run as the caller's hooks, so its state gets mixed up with the caller's as soon as the call becomes conditional. Render it with JSX instead.

The rule looks inside components and hooks. It reports a call to a capitalized function that comes from outside the component, and a call to a capitalized method such as `ui.Avatar()`. All-caps functions such as `T()` and built-ins such as `Number()`, `String()` and `BigInt()` are allowed.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react-hooks/capitalized-calls" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
import Avatar from "./Avatar";

function Profile({ user }) {
  return <section>{Avatar({ user })}</section>;
}
```

{/* bad */}
```jsx
import * as ui from "./ui";

function Profile({ user }) {
  return <section>{ui.Avatar({ user })}</section>;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
import Avatar from "./Avatar";
import { T } from "./translate";

function Profile({ user }) {
  const age = Number(user.age);
  return (
    <section>
      <Avatar user={user} />
      {T("profile.age")}: {String(age)}
    </section>
  );
}
```

{/* good */}
```jsx
function Profile({ user }) {
  const id = BigInt(user.id);
  return <section>{String(id)}</section>;
}
```

With an ESLint config, `BigInt()` and `Symbol()` are reported, like they are in `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`.

## Options

With an oxlint config, `react/capitalized-calls` takes an object that names the capitalized functions that aren't components. With `bunfig.toml` or an ESLint config the object does nothing.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `allow` | Names of functions that can be called. |
| `allowPattern` | A regular expression, as a string. A function can be called if the pattern matches anywhere in its name. |

```json .oxlintrc.json
{
  "plugins": ["react"],
  "rules": {
    "react/capitalized-calls": ["error", { "allow": ["Avatar"], "allowPattern": "Event$" }]
  }
}
```

{/* good {"config": "oxlint", "options": [{"allow": ["Avatar"]}]} */}
```jsx
import Avatar from "./Avatar";

function Profile({ user }) {
  return <section>{Avatar({ user })}</section>;
}
```

{/* good {"config": "oxlint", "options": [{"allowPattern": "Event$"}]} */}
```jsx
import { ClickEvent } from "./events";

function SaveButton({ track }) {
  const event = ClickEvent("save");
  return <button onClick={() => track(event)}>Save</button>;
}
```

Both options are about functions. A capitalized method such as `ui.Avatar()` is reported whatever they say.

`allowPattern` is a pattern for Rust's `regex` crate, as in oxlint, not a JavaScript one. It can't have lookahead or backreferences. It can have what only that crate has, such as `(?x)` for blanks and comments, `(?P<name>..)` and `[[:upper:]]`:

{/* good {"config": "oxlint", "options": [{"allowPattern": "(?x) ^ [[:upper:]] [[:lower:]]+ Event $  # a name that ends in Event"}]} */}
```jsx
import { ClickEvent } from "./events";

function SaveButton({ track }) {
  const event = ClickEvent("save");
  return <button onClick={() => track(event)}>Save</button>;
}
```

A name in `\p{..}` is read as the crate reads it. Case, spaces, `_` and `-` don't count, and neither does `is` before the name, so `\p{lu}`, `\p{IsLu}` and `\p{uppercase letter}` are all `\p{Lu}`:

{/* good {"config": "oxlint", "options": [{"allowPattern": "^\\p{lu}\\p{isLower}+Event$"}]} */}
```jsx
import { ClickEvent } from "./events";

function SaveButton({ track }) {
  const event = ClickEvent("save");
  return <button onClick={() => track(event)}>Save</button>;
}
```

Some classes that the crate has aren't supported. A pattern with one of them allows nothing, and no message says so. oxlint allows what the pattern matches. They are:

- `\p{Age=..}`, `\p{Grapheme_Cluster_Break=..}`, `\p{Sentence_Break=..}` and `\p{Word_Break=..}`, also when the property is written `age`, `gcb`, `sb` or `wb`
- the binary properties `Grapheme_Link`, `Hyphen`, `IDS_Unary_Operator`, `ID_Compat_Math_Continue`, `ID_Compat_Math_Start`, `Modifier_Combining_Mark`, `Other_Alphabetic`, `Other_Default_Ignorable_Code_Point`, `Other_Grapheme_Extend`, `Other_ID_Continue`, `Other_ID_Start`, `Other_Lowercase`, `Other_Math`, `Other_Uppercase` and `Prepended_Concatenation_Mark`

## When not to use it

If your code has plain functions with capitalized names, such as factories, every call to them from a component is reported. Rename them, allow them with the options above, or leave the rule off.
